content:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT triggered: GPU pool us-east-1-prod - queue_length > 1200 for 2m, throttling started. Pager: @sanjay (on-call)

sanjay: I'm on it, jumping in. any customer-impact details?

linda: seeing elevated 503/429 on hosted API, dashboard shows token_throttle spikes and increased avg queue wait. A few high-volume customers reporting errors.

maria: support: ticket #C-4321 and #C-4322 opened; customers reporting slow responses and intermittent 503s. Estimated affected traffic ~6% of requests in us-east-1.

eli: digging into autoscaler logs now. quick telemetry: GPU utilization per node has dropped ~10% while queue length increased. suspicious.

ops-bot: autoscaler: attempted scale at 1808501300 -> requested +4 nodes, but scale denied: reached configured max_nodes=8.

kevin: wait we had a quota bump last month to 12 for dedicated pools.. why is max_nodes 8? any recent config change?

linda: checking infra config history... I see a config rollout 1808499000 for "runtime-batching-v2" that touched autoscaler-policy and batching defaults.

sanjay: paste relevant logs/snips please.

eli: pasting relevant logs:

```
[1808501255] queue_len=210 -> queue_len=420 -> queue_len=900
[1808501280] autoscaler: evaluate -> desired_nodes=12, current_nodes=8, max_nodes=8 -> scale_denied
[1808501292] runtime: batch_hit_rate=0.26, prefix_cache_miss=74%, continuous_batch_size_avg=6
[1808501296] runtime: per_token_cpu_time inc, per_token_gpu_time dec, observed small-batch overheads
[1808501304] runtime-error: prefix_cache_key_normalizer changed: include-session=true
```

eli: the rollout changed prefix cache normalization and continuous batching defaults. looks like cache keys now include ephemeral session ids -> cache miss explosion. continuous batching size dropped and we're getting many small batches. small batches reduce GPU throughput and confuse autoscaler heuristics which use aggregated compute_time. autoscaler sees low compute_time per node so it doesn't want to scale beyond max_nodes (and max_nodes was lowered in the same rollout).

maria: customers are in the loop, initial SLO impact message sent. Support is triaging priority customers.

sanjay: immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert the runtime-batching-v2 rollout (flag rollback) 2) temporarily raise autoscaler max_nodes to 16 3) manually add +4 GPUs to us-east-1 pool 4) enable emergency prefix_cache override true

kevin: agree. which is fastest?

eli: fastest is flag flip for prefix_cache normalization to previous behavior -> I'll patch the feature flag and push. Then we need a revert of the autoscaler-policy change.

linda: I'm on rollback PR for runtime-batching-v2 to flip continuous_batch_window_ms back to 25ms and restore prefix cache key normalizer. drafting now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback job queued: runtime-batching-v2 revert -> target services: runtime-prod-us-east-1 -> estimated impact: 2-3m per node restart.

sanjay: ops, pls bump max_nodes asap. Eli, can you do manual capacity add while rollback is in flight?

eli: I'm provisioning 4 nodes now (manual hot-add). ETA 7m. Also patching autoscaler config to set max_nodes=16.

support-bot: Notifying customers in impacted region: message template queued. Will send updates at 15m intervals.

linda: rollback PR merged, starting rollout to runtime-prod-us-east-1. will monitor traffic and batch metrics.

(5m pass)

eli: manual nodes are up. autoscaler max_nodes set to 16. queue length trending down from 1200 -> 420. prefix_cache_miss trending down from 74% -> 18%. continuous_batch_size_avg rising back to ~32.

maria: support: customers reporting improvement, 2 customers confirm throughput restored. Still tracking one large customer with regex-based prompts that used the broken normalizer.

sanjay: good. keep rollout until all nodes back to healthy metrics. assign a DER (do-not-deploy) tag to runtime-batching-v2 until postmortem.

kevin: open action items: (1) postmortem + root cause (2) tighten deploy gates around cache-key changes (3) autoscaler policy review - don't co-deploy batching and scale policy changes together (4) add alert for prefix_cache_miss > 40%

linda: noted, creating incident ticket INC-2026-317 and adding action items.

eli: quick note: autoscaler metric pipeline used compute_time that is sensitive to batch size. we'll add derived metric gpu_bytes_per_sec and queue-backed desired_nodes estimation to avoid small-batch blindspots. adding to action items.

maria: sending second customer update: mitigation in place, monitoring, postmortem promised in 48h.

sanjay: handing off to night on-call @eli in 30m. I'll stay for the handoff.

eli: taking over monitoring. current state: queue_len ~120 -> target steady state <50, prefix_cache_miss 12%, continuous_batch_size_avg 30, 200 nodes allocated? (typo... 12 nodes allocated). I'll escalate if we see re-regression.

sanjay: thanks. please file a follow-up RFC for safer rollout process and include automated canary checks for cache-hit regressions.

ops-bot: incident status updated -> mitigated, severity downgraded to SEV-2.

maria: I'll schedule customer debriefs for affected accounts.

kevin: kudos to the team for quick rollback. we'll want to include timeline + diff in the postmortem.

linda: creating timeline notes now and saving logs. Will include the rollout diff that changed prefix cache normalizer and autoscaler-policy max_nodes param.

sanjay: end of handoff. leaving the channel open for any escalations. next steps: postmortem, deploy gate changes, new autoscaler metrics, alert for prefix cache miss.

eli: acknowledged - will own on-call follow-ups.

support-bot: Incident channel archived at 1808504834. Postmortem stubs: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/INC-2026-317
